vignette: Kofi had always known that his childhood was different. Growing up in a traditional Ghanaian household with strict rules and expectations, he learned early on to navigate the complexities of family dynamics. But it wasn't until much later, as an adult looking back, that Kofi began to realize just how far-reaching the effects of those years would be. Kofi's father, a man known for his fiery temper and unyielding discipline, had been a constant source of fear in their home. One particular incident stood out in Kofi's mind - though it was fragmented, like a puzzle with missing pieces. He remembered being around 8 or 9 years old, playing outside when he broke one of the family rules. His father's reaction was swift and merciless: Kofi recalled feeling the sting of his father's belt on his skin, but the specifics were hazy. What lingered instead was the overwhelming sense of helplessness that had washed over him in that moment. Years went by, but Kofi never spoke about what happened. Old photos would occasionally resurface, showing happier times - his parents smiling, family gatherings - and Kofi's mind would instinctively recoil from them. He found it difficult to deliberately recall the memories of those years; trying only made his head spin with anxious thoughts. As he grew older, Kofi learned to avoid situations that felt unpredictable or outside his control. As a principal at a local school, he thrived on routine and order - qualities he had lacked in his own childhood. But even this carefully constructed sense of stability couldn't shield him from the occasional nightmare. Waking up drenched in sweat, with images of chaos still seared into his mind's eye, would leave Kofi shaken for hours. Kofi was terrified that one day, his own anger would boil over and he'd lose control, just like his father before him. This fear simmered beneath the surface of his relationships, including his current partnership. His girlfriend noticed how tightly wound he was at times, but Kofi couldn't quite explain why - even to himself. He felt permanently changed for the worse by what had happened in those childhood years. The memories still lingered with a vividness that normal recollections lacked. When they bubbled up unbidden, as they sometimes did during quiet moments or when old photos resurfaced, Kofi's thoughts would grow muddled and he'd retreat into himself. It was only recently, after an argument with his girlfriend had left him feeling lost and shaken, that Kofi realized just how far these symptoms had carried over into his adult life. He began to recognize patterns of avoidance, the way certain triggers could still transport him back to those days when helplessness seemed absolute. With a dawning sense of trepidation, Kofi sought out therapy, unsure what lay ahead but certain that he couldn't keep living this way - haunted by memories and forever on edge. He wanted to understand why his past continued to hold such sway over him, and how to build a life where those fragmented pieces could finally be set aside.
